rationale: Both reviews independently surface the one live ground-truth concern (FLASHINFER_ATTN allow-listed for quant with no consumer, silently dropping the config) with strong grounding, and both correctly note the sage-kwargs-unconditional issue is already fixed in this diff. X is more polished and gives ready-to-paste code fixes, but one 'blocking' finding (output dtype change) leans on unverifiable FlashInfer-internal line citations not present in the diff or repo, a fabrication risk. Y's evidence-quote methodology (verbatim greps for every claim) is more consistently verifiable and surfaces a genuinely valuable, non-obvious catch X misses entirely — the four new SAGE unit tests inheriting a module-level `cuda` pytestmark, so they're silently deselected from the CPU-only CI lane. Y's remediation language is slightly less copy-paste-ready than X's inline code snippets, keeping actionability a touch lower.
